text.arabic_uthmani: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَكْبَرُوٓا۟ إِنَّا كُلٌّۭ فِيهَآ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ حَكَمَ بَيْنَ ٱلْعِبَادِ

words.gloss_range: opening speech verb that launches the arrogant group reply as one quoted answer and carries both admission and verdict inside that speech frame
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, declaration, verbal stance, and exchange range; the local Form I active selects direct accountable saying rather than causative, reciprocal, or passive report

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: completed adjudication that closes the reply
certifying particle before the verdict verb
first emphatic admission inside the quoted reply
totality inside the first assertion
locative predicate of shared containment

words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) opens by making the answer a speech event before the plural speakers are fully named. The singular verb compresses the arrogant group into one reply-position, then its scope carries both {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:innā}}) {{ar:كُلٌّۭ}} ({{tr:kullun}}) {{ar:فِيهَآ}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) and the later verdict clause inside the same defeated answer. The root remains direct accountable saying, not imposed speech through a causative making-say form or bargaining through a reciprocal bargaining form; human speech begins the ayah, but {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) and {{ar:حَكَمَ}} ({{tr:ḥakama}}) make that speech yield to completed judgment.

topics.headline: singular verb makes one collective reply
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears many arrogant speakers reduced to one unified reply-position before their words unfold.
topics.reason: The singular perfect verb precedes and is resolved by the plural relative subject, so the reply is front-loaded as one speech act.

topics.headline: speech becomes public admission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the former superior group is made audible as responsible speakers who concede confinement in their own reply.
topics.reason: The active Form I speech verb keeps the speakers visible and turns their answer into a stated stance.

topics.headline: direct saying rather than bargaining
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer is not negotiation or assigned wording; it is direct speech already bounded by the verdict that follows.
topics.reason: The local form is simple active speech, not causative or reciprocal speech, and the following verdict closes exchange rather than reopening it.

topics.headline: reply answers the prior plea
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah as the answer to the plea in 40:47, with both clauses held inside one quoted response.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the whole remaining ayah the quoted complement of the opening speech verb, and the boundary rows tie it to the prior request in 40:47.

topics.headline: human reply yields to divine verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a movement from human answering to certified judgment, reinforced by repeated hard sounds across the reply.
topics.reason: The speech verb and judgment clause are both local, while the same-surah speech-chain and sound rows add a coherent discourse and cadence payoff.

words.gloss_range: masculine plural relative pronoun that makes the following arrogance clause the speakers’ identifying label and resumes the group addressed in 40:47

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the relative-clause action that identifies the group

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not introduce a neutral crowd. It makes the following {{ar:ٱسْتَكْبَرُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:istakbarū}}) the group label, so every word of the reply is heard through the identity already assigned to the speakers. The same relative description also carries the group from the appeal in 40:47 into the answer here, changing them from addressed party to answering subject.

topics.headline: relative clause defines the speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers are grammatically classified by their arrogant action before the quotation begins.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is the subject of the speech verb and requires the following relative clause to complete the identifying label.

topics.headline: appealed-to group becomes subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees continuity with 40:47: the same arrogant group that was appealed to now answers.
topics.reason: The cross-reference evidence resolves the definite relative description as the group addressed by the weak in 40:47.

topics.headline: moral label frames the quote
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the quoted content as speech from a morally classified group, not as an anonymous factual statement.
topics.reason: The identity label precedes the quoted content and therefore frames the admission before it is spoken.

words.gloss_range: Form X plural perfect active self-exalting action used as the relative-clause identity of the speakers, later flattened by shared containment and servant status
words.root_gloss_range: greatness, size, seniority, weight, and arrogance range; the local Form X selects sought or claimed greatness as blameworthy self-exaltation rather than neutral greatness

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: unrestricted totality that cancels elite exception
servant identity under judgment
shared enclosure that answers claimed elevation

words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْتَكْبَرُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:istakbarū}}) completes the speaker label before the quotation begins, so the answer starts under the sign of self-exaltation. Form X makes greatness a sought or claimed status rather than simple bigness through bare greatness, and the active plural form keeps the speakers responsible for that posture. This status dispute also resembles the arrogant-and-weak confrontation at judgment (34:31-33) and continues the same role shift from 40:47 into 40:48. The reply then reverses the posture: {{ar:كُلٌّۭ}} ({{tr:kullun}}) and {{ar:فِيهَآ}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) flatten claimed height into shared containment, while {{ar:ٱلْعِبَادِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿibād}}) leaves the final identity as dependent servanthood.

topics.headline: arrogance completes the subject label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speech source is not complete until arrogant action has named who they are.
topics.reason: The relative clause is syntactically tied to the relative pronoun and comes immediately before the quoted admission.

topics.headline: self-exalting agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees arrogance as their own completed moral posture, not as a neutral rank or passive status.
topics.reason: The perfect active Form X verb presents the prior self-exalting act as an accountable identifier.

topics.headline: Form X sought greatness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word marks claimed or pursued greatness, while local context keeps it in the blameworthy arrogance branch.
topics.reason: The root range includes size and greatness more broadly, but the local Form X verb and discourse context select arrogant self-magnification.

topics.headline: claimed height meets shared containment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the vertical claim of greatness answered by everyone being inside the same enclosure.
topics.reason: The local first quoted clause places the arrogant group inside the same totality and location that defeats the height claim.

topics.headline: arrogant and weak confrontation continues
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reply as part of a recurring status dispute, especially the direct movement from the challenged group in 40:47 to the answering group in 40:48.
topics.reason: The concrete rows tie the word to the prior ayah and to comparable judgment confrontations without replacing the local parse.

topics.headline: self-magnification answered by servants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from self-exalting identity to servant identity as its final reversal.
topics.reason: The opening identity and final noun are both local, and their contrast states the ayah-level status reversal.

words.gloss_range: emphatic first-person plural opening of the quote, fusing assertion with self-inclusion before widening through totality and location

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: totality that widens the speaker pronoun
second emphatic particle introducing the ground

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:innā}}) begins the quoted content with assertion and self-inclusion at once. The attached pronoun makes the arrogant speakers put themselves inside the claim before {{ar:كُلٌّۭ}} ({{tr:kullun}}) widens it to all parties, and the nominal clause presents containment as a standing condition rather than a new event. The later {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) repeats the emphatic frame but shifts from admitted state to the ground of that state: God has already judged.

topics.headline: assertion and self-inclusion fused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the former elites include themselves before explaining anything about others.
topics.reason: The particle plus attached first-person plural pronoun is the governed noun of emphasis and opens the admission.

topics.headline: speaker pronoun widens through totality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from our condition to everyone’s condition within one clause.
topics.reason: The following totality word broadens the speaker reference while retaining the fact that the confession is spoken by one side.

topics.headline: nominal clause as standing state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels shared containment as an established condition, not a fresh event being narrated.
topics.reason: The first quoted assertion is a nominal clause without an overt finite verb after the particle.

topics.headline: admission followed by ground
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reply shaped as emphatic admission first and legal explanation second.
topics.reason: The two emphatic openings and the certification particle produce a two-beat quoted reply calibrated to close the prior expectation.

words.gloss_range: unpossessed nominative totality after the speaker pronoun, making inclusion independent and exhaustive before the locative predicate specifies the enclosure
words.root_gloss_range: totality, every member, completion, and encirclement range; the local noun selects exhaustive inclusion with enclosure pressure, not a separate root-wide claim beyond the clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: speaker-bound admission widened by totality
locative predicate that places the total set inside the known fire
later distinction among those included

words.prose: {{ar:كُلٌّۭ}} ({{tr:kullun}}) turns the speakers’ {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:innā}}) into unrestricted totality before {{ar:فِيهَآ}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) gives that totality a place. Its suffixless, nominative form no longer says the prior possessive you-all totality in 40:47; it states an unpossessed all that includes the speakers and blocks elite exception. Against a pattern where divided groups are gathered back despite division (21:93-94), this allness gathers weak and arrogant into one punishment state. The encirclement pressure of the root makes the allness feel enclosing, while the later {{ar:بَيْنَ}} ({{tr:bayna}}) prevents that shared fate from erasing differentiated judgment among servants.

topics.headline: unpossessed all includes speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from the prior you-all accusation in 40:47 to an unrestricted all confessed by the arrogant themselves.
topics.reason: The local noun lacks a possessive suffix, unlike the boundary wording from 40:47, so totality is no longer factionally addressed.

topics.headline: nominative totality stands forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears allness as part of the statement itself, not merely as a circumstantial aside.
topics.reason: The canonical nominative can function appositionally or predicate-like after the particle; the shawadhdh accusative contrast is useful as apparatus but does not govern the local parse.

topics.headline: encirclement pressure in total inclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels totality as complete enclosure that cancels hierarchy, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as exhaustive allness.
topics.reason: The root range supports encircling pressure, but the local noun functions as totality in the clause rather than as an independent physical act.

topics.headline: allness answers status hierarchy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the emphatic totality is calibrated to the contested hierarchy: claimed elevation is answered by shared inclusion inside the fire.
topics.reason: The local sequence joins the arrogance label, emphatic admission, totality, and locative predicate into one reversal.

topics.headline: allness held with later between-ness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the ayah can gather all parties into one fate while later distinguishing them under judgment.
topics.reason: The concrete 21:93-94 contrast and the local later between-word support a gathering-with-distinction payoff without changing the local totality parse.

topics.headline: totality bridges pronoun to location
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels allness pause as the hinge between self-reference and enclosure before the location is supplied.
topics.reason: The word stands between the speaker pronoun and the locative predicate, and the nunated ending gives that totalizing unit audible weight.

words.gloss_range: prepositional predicate with feminine pronoun, recovering the fire from 40:47 and making shared inclusion both location and condition

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the fire from 40:47 recovered by this word’s feminine pronoun
the total set whose predicate is this locative phrase

words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَآ}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) completes the first assertion by putting the whole set inside the known fire. The feminine pronoun has to be recovered from {{ar:ٱلنَّارِ}} ({{tr:al-nār}}) in 40:47, so the reply remains anchored to the very domain from which relief was requested. Because the phrase functions as predicate, being in it is the core claim; {{ar:فِيهَآ}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) lets the fire be both enclosing place and irreversible condition.

topics.headline: inside-it completes totality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that totality becomes concrete only when the phrase places everyone inside the known domain.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the phrase as the predicate of the first quoted assertion.

topics.headline: pronoun carries the fire across boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the answer tied directly to the fire named in 40:47, not to an unspecified place.
topics.reason: The feminine pronoun has no local antecedent within 40:48 and therefore recovers the fire from the prior ayah.

topics.headline: location becomes condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fire is not only a place they occupy but the condition that defines the reply.
topics.reason: The preposition can mark spatial and situational inclusion, and the fire antecedent licenses both as local payoff.

topics.headline: preposition and pronoun fused
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the admission as compressed and immediate, without a separate verb slowing the enclosure claim.
topics.reason: The preposition and suffix are one surface unit, and the nominal clause omits an overt copula.

words.gloss_range: second emphatic particle opening a separate explanatory clause whose governed divine name grounds the prior shared-containment claim

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first emphatic admission of shared state
certification particle stacked with the second emphasis
divine name governed by the second emphatic particle

words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) starts a fresh emphatic clause rather than simply extending the first. Unlike fused {{ar:إِنَّا}} ({{tr:innā}}), this standalone particle opens around {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}), moving the answer from the speakers’ included state to the external authority that explains it. Its direct, asyndetic arrival and its pairing with {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) make the second half of the quote a legal ground, not a renewed negotiation.

topics.headline: second emphasis grounds the admission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reply move from shared containment to the reason it cannot be negotiated: divine judgment.
topics.reason: The second particle governs the divine name and scopes the whole judgment clause as a separate explanatory assertion.

topics.headline: from fused speaker claim to divine-name clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a formal shift from speaker-bound admission to an authority-centered clause.
topics.reason: The second particle is not fused to a pronoun and introduces a new governed noun.

topics.headline: emphasis plus certification closes doubt
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the answer as declarative closure rather than an offer, condition, or counter-request.
topics.reason: The second emphatic clause combines with the certification particle and perfect judgment verb to answer a disputed expectation.

topics.headline: no connector tightens cause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second assertion follows directly as explanation rather than as a loosely coordinated add-on.
topics.reason: The second clause begins without a coordinating connector, so the explanatory relation is syntactically tight.

words.gloss_range: the proper divine name foregrounded after the second emphatic particle as the unique semantic agent of the completed judgment
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name range tied to worship-worthy authority, devotion, dependence, possible derivational awe or bewilderment, and exaltedness; the local proper noun selects the named divine judge, not a generic deity noun

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the judgment action for which the divine name is semantic agent
servants under the named judge
second emphatic particle governing the divine name

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) is foregrounded immediately after the second {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}), before the act of judgment is named. Although the particle gives it accusative case, the following {{ar:حَكَمَ}} ({{tr:ḥakama}}) makes God the semantic agent, so the grammar does not weaken agency. The proper name is not a generic deity noun; in this reply it identifies the unique judge whose authority turns former social ranks into {{ar:ٱلْعِبَادِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿibād}}). The exclusive-judgment principle is enacted as a closed case here (12:40), while the same surah later keeps promise, forgiveness, and praise grounded in God (40:55). The contested derivational pressures around worship-worthy authority, dependence, and exaltedness survive as pressure around the named judge, while the local form remains the proper divine name.

topics.headline: divine name before judgment verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the judge before the action, so the cause of containment is centered outside both factions.
topics.reason: The proper noun is governed by the second emphatic particle and stands before the predicate verb that reports completed judgment.

topics.headline: case governance does not weaken agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that grammatical accusative under the particle and semantic agency in the verdict coexist.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the divine name the semantic subject of the judgment verb despite its particle-governed case.

topics.headline: proper name blocks generic deity reading
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the judgment anchored in the named divine authority, not in a general class of deity or authority.
topics.reason: The aligned word is a proper noun rather than an indefinite common noun.

topics.headline: worship and dependence pressures converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels worship-worthy authority, dependent turning, and exaltedness converging around judgment, while the local word remains the proper divine name.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute can color the authority relation, but it does not replace the local proper-name reading.

topics.headline: exclusive judgment doctrine becomes scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the principle that judgment belongs to God enacted in this closed dispute (12:40).
topics.reason: Concrete inter-ayah rows connect the divine-name judgment pair to exclusivity language and same-surah authority without overriding the local clause.

topics.headline: judge and servants frame the relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final relation becoming vertical: God judges, and all disputed parties end as servants.
topics.reason: The divine name, judgment verb, and servant noun are all local and converge to replace social obligation with completed authority.

words.gloss_range: certification and aspect particle directly before the perfect judgment verb, marking the verdict as already realized and specifically scoped to that act

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: perfect judgment verb certified by this particle
emphatic particle stacked with certification

words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) stands directly before {{ar:حَكَمَ}} ({{tr:ḥakama}}), so closure arrives before the judgment verb itself is heard. Its force is tightly scoped to the perfect act of judgment, not to the whole reply in a loose way. Together with {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}), it makes the prior request in 40:47 too late for bargaining: the verdict has already been realized.

topics.headline: already-realized verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the judgment is presented as already settled, so appeal is no longer pending.
topics.reason: The particle precedes a perfect verb and is identified as certification and aspect before the judgment act.

topics.headline: particle scopes to following perfect
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle certifies the judgment act specifically rather than vaguely intensifying everything around it.
topics.reason: The uninflected particle is placed directly before the perfect verb and modifies that predicate.

topics.headline: assertion plus certification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears finality before the verb, as if negotiation is syntactically preempted.
topics.reason: The second emphatic particle and this certification particle combine in the same judgment clause.

topics.headline: local dispute broadened to servants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the specific shared-fire admission broaden into a general statement about judgment among servants.
topics.reason: The certified judgment clause follows the specific confinement statement and ends with a broad servant class.

words.gloss_range: Form I perfect active judgment by God with a between-complement, selecting completed direct adjudication of relations rather than delegated arbitration or mutual litigation
words.root_gloss_range: judging, deciding, restraining disorder, firming, wisdom, and secure ordering range; the local Form I perfect with between-complement selects direct completed adjudication that stabilizes contested relations

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: certification of completed judgment
between-complement that makes relation the adjudicated field
semantic subject of the judgment verb

words.prose: {{ar:حَكَمَ}} ({{tr:ḥakama}}) is the short perfect verb that seals the reply. With {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) before it and {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) as semantic subject, judgment is direct and completed; there is no passive, delegated-arbitration, or mutual-litigation frame. Because the verb governs {{ar:بَيْنَ}} ({{tr:bayna}}) rather than a simple object, the contested relation among parties is what gets settled. The commanded duty to judge between people justly (4:58) and the request for God to judge between servants (39:46) return here as completed divine outcome. The root’s firmness and restraint pressure makes the verdict feel like ordering a disputed space, not merely announcing a sentence.

topics.headline: perfect active divine judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees God as the direct agent of a completed judgment even though the subject is not repeated in the verb phrase.
topics.reason: The perfect active verb follows the divine name and is certified by the preceding particle.

topics.headline: judgment targets relations among parties
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that judgment is cast across relations among parties, not as a simple direct object verdict.
topics.reason: The verb takes the between-phrase as relational complement and no direct object.

topics.headline: ruling as stabilizing contested space
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the judgment as firm ordering of a disputed relation, while local grammar keeps verdict as the selected action.
topics.reason: The root range supports firmness, restraint, and ordering, but the local verb is the judgment act in a certified clause.

topics.headline: no delegated or mutual arbitration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices no intermediary judge or open litigation scene: the form assigns the decisive act directly to God.
topics.reason: The aligned surface is Form I active perfect, not a delegated or mutual derivative.

topics.headline: between-servants formula accomplished
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a known judgment-between formula appearing as accomplished verdict rather than request (39:46; 4:58).
topics.reason: The concrete rows compare commanded or requested judgment elsewhere with the completed judgment wording here.

topics.headline: short verdict cuts off appeal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final adjudication beat shut down the prior social appeal while preserving the party relation through the between-complement.
topics.reason: The verb sits after the emphatic and aspect particles and before the relational complement, making it the pivot from plea to settled verdict.

words.gloss_range: construct adverbial between-complement after the judgment verb, making relation among the servants the judged field and preserving distinction inside shared containment
words.root_gloss_range: between, interval, separation, relation, clarity, and distinction range; the local adverbial construct selects relational domain among parties while clarity pressure survives as adjudicated distinction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: judgment verb governed with this between-complement
genitive complement completing the construct
earlier totality balanced by later distinction

words.prose: {{ar:بَيْنَ}} ({{tr:bayna}}) keeps the judgment from becoming an undifferentiated mass outcome. As an adverbial construct after {{ar:حَكَمَ}} ({{tr:ḥakama}}), it waits for {{ar:ٱلْعِبَادِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿibād}}) to complete the phrase and makes relation among servants the field of judgment. The judgment-between-servants formula requested elsewhere (39:46) appears here as answer rather than request. After {{ar:كُلٌّۭ}} ({{tr:kullun}}) has gathered everyone inside the fire, {{ar:بَيْنَ}} ({{tr:bayna}}) brings back distinction: shared containment remains, but cases and relations are clarified under the verdict.

topics.headline: between bound to servants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the judged field is a completed relation among servants, not an abstract between-space.
topics.reason: The word is an adverbial construct head completed by the following genitive noun.

topics.headline: multiple parties preserved
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees multiple sides preserved inside the verdict rather than a single object being judged.
topics.reason: The judgment verb has no direct object and takes the between-complement.

topics.headline: between-ness counters allness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that everyone is included in the same fate, yet judgment still distinguishes positions within it.
topics.reason: The root range supports separation and clarity, while the local sequence places between-ness after totality.

topics.headline: speech becomes judged relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reply naming the relational field already judged, with the judgment-between-servants formula fulfilled (39:46).
topics.reason: The concrete 39:46 row and the local speech-to-between sequence support formula fulfillment without replacing local syntax.

topics.headline: relation delayed before final class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels attention suspended on relation just before the final noun names the judged class.
topics.reason: The penultimate construct word is incomplete until the final noun, and the cadence lengthens into closure.

topics.headline: negotiated relation becomes judged
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the former leader-follower relation transformed into a legal-divine relation.
topics.reason: The boundary row coheres with the local move from social appeal to judgment among servants.

words.gloss_range: definite plural genitive servant noun completing the between-construct, naming the judged class and closing the reply by reclassifying former ranks as dependent servants
words.root_gloss_range: worship, service, servanthood, subjection, dependence, and accountable subjecthood range; the local plural selects servants or dependent subjects under God rather than only ritual worshippers

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: construct head completed by this genitive noun
self-exalting identity reversed by servant identity
divine judge before whom the class stands

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعِبَادِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿibād}}) completes {{ar:بَيْنَ}} ({{tr:bayna}}) and gives the ayah its landing point. The definite genitive plural names a known judged class, not an unspecified indefinite servant class, and the servant field selects accountable dependence before God rather than only ritual worship identity. The servant term also closes the judgment-among-servants formula as fulfilled in this infernal argument (39:46). By ending here, the reply reclassifies the people introduced through {{ar:ٱسْتَكْبَرُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:istakbarū}}): former leader and follower ranks are absorbed into servant-status under the completed judgment.

topics.headline: final noun defines judged arena
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final noun is grammatically necessary to define among whom judgment has occurred.
topics.reason: The word is definite plural genitive and completes the construct headed by the previous word.

topics.headline: servants as accountable dependents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees all parties named as dependent subjects before God, while local context keeps the sense broader than ritual worshippers alone.
topics.reason: The root range includes worship and subjection, but the judgment clause selects servant dependence under divine authority.

topics.headline: servanthood answers self-exaltation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s frame turning self-exalting identity into dependent servant identity.
topics.reason: The opening arrogance label and final servant noun form a local status-reversal frame.

topics.headline: plural servant class absorbs ranks
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees former faction labels replaced by one known dependent class under judgment.
topics.reason: The definite plural servant noun is used instead of repeating the arrogant faction label or introducing an indefinite class.

topics.headline: servants close the judgment formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final noun as the closing term of a divine judgment-among-servants formula (39:46).
topics.reason: The concrete row ties the servant noun to the judgment-between-servants formula, locally completed by the preceding words.

topics.headline: servant identity as endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader leaves the ayah with dependence before God, not arrogance, weakness, or former hierarchy, as the closing classification.
topics.reason: The word is the ayah-final noun and carries the cadence and boundary payoff of reclassifying the disputed parties.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The k-b-r marked speakers answer with the totalizing k-l-l expression and a shared locative pronoun.
baseline_models.mechanism: A self-elevating class speaks, but comprehensive inclusion in one enclosure removes the spatial privilege its rank presumed.

activation_trace.role: Self-magnification supplies the hierarchy whose claimed elevation is cancelled by common containment.
Comprehensive inclusion gathers every member of the speaking group into one condition.

changed_reading.before: The speakers merely report that everyone is in the same place.
changed_reading.after: Their sentence is a forced admission that the hierarchy they built cannot secure a different place for its upper tier.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The focus places comprehensive k-l-l beside the h-k-m verb and the relational b-y-n construction.
baseline_models.mechanism: Total co-presence and adjudicative separation operate at once: sharing a location does not erase distinctions among the persons judged.

activation_trace.role: Wholeness supplies exhaustive membership in the shared condition.
Judicial decision supplies the act that assigns relations and outcomes among persons.
Separation after association prevents shared placement from becoming undifferentiated identity.
The interval among multiple parties provides the relational field in which judgment operates.

changed_reading.before: Comprehensive presence merges the parties into one undifferentiated collective.
changed_reading.after: The focus holds sameness of location together with judicial differentiation among the people located there.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Self-elevating speakers name God as judge and describe the judged parties through the a-b-d noun.
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers' own grammar relocates superior and subordinate beneath one owner and object of obedience, undoing their claim to sovereign rank.

activation_trace.role: Rank and headship supply the social elevation that the utterance relinquishes.
The worshipped one supplies the authority above every human rank.
Owned servanthood places all disputants below the judging owner.
Submissive obedience supplies the relation that self-exaltation had denied.

changed_reading.before: The former superiors identify who issued the judgment.
changed_reading.after: In identifying the judge, they also reclassify themselves and their followers as co-servants rather than rival sovereigns.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: An answering q-w-l act terminates in the assertion that judgment has already occurred.
baseline_models.mechanism: Speech begins as negotiation between parties but invokes a completed restraining decision, converting the reply into closure rather than a new exercise of control.

activation_trace.role: Mutual discussion supplies the live bargaining frame in which this answer is delivered.
Restraint that blocks harmful action makes the prior ruling a limit on further intervention.
Adjudication supplies the completed decision that closes the exchange.

changed_reading.before: The reply gives information about a divine verdict.
changed_reading.after: The reply also closes bargaining: those once able to issue orders now cite a prior ruling that prevents them from acting.

context_deltas.mechanism: Followers ask former superiors to absorb or remove an assigned portion; the totalizing reply reveals that rank contains no surplus capacity with which punishment can be redistributed.

activation_trace.role: Leadership and elevated rank anchor the addressees as the former patrons.
Comprehensive inclusion denies an exempt upper tier from which aid could be transferred.
Ordered allegiance supplies the earlier leader-dependent bond now being tested.
Lack of strength identifies the dependent side of the failed hierarchy.
Sufficiency and protective capacity define exactly what followers ask the leaders to provide.
An assigned share supplies the proposed unit of transfer or reduction.

structural_cues: The immediately preceding turn moves from subordinate appeal to superior reply and asks whether a defined part of the same penalty can be removed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies allegiance, weakness, sufficiency, and an assigned share; I infer that hierarchy had functioned as promised protection and that common containment cancels its transfer capacity. A live alternative is that the leaders merely refuse, but their exhaustive answer favors inability.

changed_reading.before: The speakers acknowledge only that leaders and followers share a destination.
changed_reading.after: They acknowledge the bankruptcy of patronage itself: superior status cannot carry, offset, or reassign even part of a follower's burden.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah's earlier judicial formula pairs each self with its own acquisition and exact accounting; therefore comprehensive co-location in the focus does not imply interchangeable agency or liability.

activation_trace.role: Total inclusion supplies common membership in the realized outcome.
Judicial decision connects the earlier accounting rule to the focus assertion.
Differentiation among associated parties preserves distinct responsibility inside common placement.
Action answered by fitting recompense supplies the judgment's distributive rule.
Each entity in its own identity supplies the unit assessed.
Acquired action supplies the person-specific basis of recompense.
Misplacing a thing from its proper setting supplies the injustice explicitly excluded from allocation.
Counting and reckoning supply the exact procedure behind the ruling.

structural_cues: An earlier day-of-judgment sequence moves from universal exposure to person-by-person recompense, excludes wrong, and ends with rapid reckoning.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a prior rule of individual recompense and the focus supplies shared placement plus judgment among parties; I infer that the earlier rule governs the later scene. A live alternative is that the focus reports location without commenting on differentiated grounds.

changed_reading.before: Because all are together, leaders and followers appear morally interchangeable.
changed_reading.after: Their common fate remains internally adjudicated: every party arrives through its own acquisition, and collective enclosure neither proves collective innocence nor identical liability.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah reserves true high rank for God, then joins human self-exaltation over worship to entry in abasement; the focus becomes the point where self-made superiors finally speak as servants under judgment.

activation_trace.role: Human self-magnification anchors the status claim reversed by the wider sequence.
Obedient servanthood names the relation the speakers had resisted.
Supreme rank and headship establish the rightful scale above human status.
Self-exaltation supplies the refusal that is explicitly opposed to worship.
Worship as submissive obedience identifies what pride rejects.
Entry into an interior supplies the realized spatial reversal of claimed elevation.
Abasement supplies the terminal posture of those who had magnified themselves.

structural_cues: The surah first locates greatness with God and later makes refusal of worship lead to entry in abasement; the focus speakers stand between those poles.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated k-b-r and a-b-d forms plus the sequence from refusal to abasement; I infer a confessional status reversal in the focus. A live alternative is thematic recurrence without conscious self-recognition, though the speakers' own servant-language supports the stronger reading.

changed_reading.before: The arrogant identify God as judge while retaining their identity as a distinct superior class.
changed_reading.after: Their answer performs a late self-demotion: the self-elevated now admit the servant category and occupy the abasement that refusal of service produced.

context_deltas.mechanism: Elsewhere divine speech is followed immediately by realized being, and the arrival of divine command is followed by conclusive true judgment; by contrast, the arrogant speakers can only report an already effective act.

activation_trace.role: An uttered statement anchors the human speech act whose force is being reassessed.
A fully secured and finalized act supplies the reality their speech can acknowledge but not alter.
An utterance immediately followed by realization supplies the contrasting model of efficacious speech.
Occurrence and presence make the commanded state follow the utterance without an implementation gap.
Binding command supplies the authority that initiates final resolution.
A cutting decision supplies the conclusive execution of that authority.
Stable correspondence with reality qualifies the executed decision as true rather than arbitrary.

structural_cues: The surah contrasts many human claims and disputes with a divine utterance that becomes reality and a divine command that arrives as executed judgment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel speech and decision events; I infer a hierarchy of speech acts in which divine saying effects reality while the leaders' saying merely registers it. A live alternative is a theological parallel without an intended contrast in performative force.

changed_reading.before: The focus opens with an ordinary report by the arrogant.
changed_reading.after: Their speech is the residue of lost command: those once obeyed can only verbalize the result of the one word and ruling that actually take effect.

context_deltas.mechanism: After followers fail to obtain relief from leaders, the condemned appeal through keepers for even a time-limited lightening; that appeal also fails, so the focus reply marks the first closed rung in an escalating chain of mediation.

activation_trace.role: Negotiating speech anchors the reply as one stage in a sequence of attempted appeals.
An imposed restraint supplies the barrier encountered at every higher rung.
Calling by speech moves the request upward after human patrons fail.
Reduction of weight defines the smaller relief sought in the second appeal.
A bounded duration reduces the request from escape to a temporary interval.
Repeated calling returns the petition to the petitioners without gaining mediation.
Departure from a destination makes the final prayer ineffective rather than merely unanswered by leaders.

structural_cues: Across the adjacent dialogue, appeal moves from followers to leaders, then from all those inside to keepers, and finally toward the Lord, while the requested relief shrinks.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered speakers and progressively smaller requests; I infer an institutional appeal chain whose every delegated layer is blocked by the completed judgment. A live alternative is that the two requests independently illustrate futility rather than form one escalation.

changed_reading.before: The leaders give a static explanation for why they will not help.
changed_reading.after: Their answer is the first failed mediation in a sequence showing that no human rank, custodian, or redirected petition can reopen the ruling.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the fire dispute, entrusting the affair to God leads to one servant's protection while punishment surrounds Pharaoh's attached house; this contrast limits the focus totality to the condemned faction rather than all servants without exception.

activation_trace.role: Comprehensive inclusion remains exhaustive while requiring its local group to be identified.
Judicial separation anchors the contrast between the protected servant and the encompassed faction.
Entrusting an affair to another supplies the protected servant's transfer of reliance to God.
Active warding of harm supplies the distinct outcome granted to that servant.
Descending harm that closes around its target supplies the opposite outcome for Pharaoh's side.
People attached to and returning to a leader define the faction later divided into superiors and followers.
Punitive pain supplies the enclosure that overtakes the attached ruling house.

structural_cues: The local sequence first separates a protected believer from Pharaoh's punished house, then depicts that house's internal leader-follower dispute.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent contrasting outcomes and then the faction's internal dispute; I infer that the focus totality is exhaustive within the condemned faction, not universal across every servant. A live alternative is that the pronoun's scope is merely local without the preceding protection scene actively delimiting it.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated totality plus expansive and surrounding roots; I infer competing or nested enclosures rather than unrelated descriptions of extent. A live alternative is that the constructions share vocabulary without forming a spatial model.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the h-k-m branch of bridle-like restraint rather than ordinary adjudication. It remains anchored in the focus verb and gains a concrete echo from later collars, linked chains, and dragging, but downstream prose should present it only as a lexical-material resonance, not as a replacement translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus h-k-m verb carried through its restraint and bridle branch.

activation_trace.role: A jaw-enclosing control that prevents free movement lets the ruling be pictured as imposed restraint.
A collar binding the body gives the abstract restraint a later material form.
Connected links extend individual restraint into an inescapable sequence.

changed_reading.before: The judgment is an abstract verdict determining relations among servants.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the verdict also becomes a controlling restraint later materialized in collars, chains, and forced movement.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it uses the packet's secondary q-w-l to q-l-l mapping, not the dominant speech root. It remains anchored in the focus's first word and is reinforced by the failed request to lighten a burden and by the contrasting effective divine utterance; render it only as wordplay about diminished or non-lifting speech.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus q-w-l occurrence through its supplied secondary q-l-l target.

activation_trace.role: Diminution lets the leaders' once-commanding speech register as a reduced, insufficient report.
Carrying and rising activate the precise capacity their answer proves unable to supply for another's burden.
Lightening a weight supplies the neighboring action that no human speech can obtain.
Ordinary utterance on the divine side introduces the counterexample of speech that is not diminished.
Immediate occurrence supplies the efficacy missing from the leaders' statement.

changed_reading.before: The leaders' utterance plainly states their inability to help.
changed_reading.after: As contained wordplay, their saying has itself become little and unable to lift, while divine saying still brings its object into being.

strongest_changes: Shared containment is a collapse of patronage and rank, not merely a shared location.
Comprehensive co-location coexists with individualized recompense and judicial separation.
The former superiors' servant-language performs a late reversal from self-exaltation to abasement.
The reply is one failed rung in an escalating appeal chain that cannot reopen completed judgment.
The statement can be true yet savingly useless because it is voiced only after the ruling is manifest.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah recurrence turns the focus into a convergence point: political and devotional hierarchy fails as protection, totality remains internally adjudicated, and human speech loses force while divine word and judgment take effect.
remaining_uncertainties: The exact local scope of the totalizing expression is inferred from the protected-person versus punished-house sequence.
The contrast between effective divine speech and merely reporting human speech is abductive rather than explicitly announced.
The nested-enclosure model may be a recurrent spatial pattern or only parallel language of extent.
The bridle-chain and secondary q-l-l activations should remain exploratory lexical resonances.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Judgment collapses the hierarchy it judges.** `ح ك م/B001` supplies restraining and setting right; `ك ب ر/B001` supplies greatness, here reflexively claimed, while “all” places both parties together. I infer that judgment corrects the false social scale by imposing shared location. The former superiors’ admission reads as forced equality under a higher ordering.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The request to custodians in 40:49 shows the hierarchy’s replacement: former leaders lose mediation, and institutional keepers become the next unsuccessfully approached layer.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Adjudication deactivates the old hierarchy's power of disposal.** Lexically, `ح ك م:B002` is "judgment and adjudication among people," with `B001` restraining and turning back to set right; `ك ل ل:B003` supplies inclusive totality. Structurally, the weak ask the proud for relief in 40:47, but the answer replaces leader/follower asymmetry with `إنا كل فيها`; 40:49 then shows that even the keepers are petitioned rather than commanding the judgment. Adjudication's role is to restrain former superiors from reallocating another's share. The packet gives the failed appeal and inclusive location; I infer that final judgment has stripped social rank of causal efficacy. The leaders' reply is thus an admission that their prior power no longer operates.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:52 removes even excuse's utility, and 40:60 makes self-magnifiers enter abased; adjudication therefore cancels both the proud leaders' rank and their remaining defensive speech.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium

branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه الخطاب اللفظي المسموع.

source_note.MU: Tekil aktarım, işitilen hitap olmaksızın içe doğan anlamın söz diye adlandırılmasını verir.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök, sesle söze dökme çekirdeğinden konuşma organı, konuşkan kişi, eski unvan, yalan isnat, söylenti, müzakere, hüküm dayatma, iç söz, görüş benimseme, sözsüz belirtme, içten önemseme, teknik tanım ve içe doğan anlam gibi ayrı dallara yayılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi azlığı çokluğun karşıtı olarak verir; ayrıca yoksulluk, düşüklük, bir şeyi az görme ve belirli yapılarda yokluğa ya da seyrekliğe yaklaşan kullanımları açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol yalnızca sayı ve miktar azlığını ve buna bağlı kullanımları kapsar; yükseklik, kap, taşıma ve titreme anlamlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Temel azlık anlamı ile yoksullaşma ve az görme gibi türemiş biçimler birlikte bulunur; yokluk ve seyrekleşme anlamları ise yalnızca belirtilen yapılara bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar azlığın temel sayı ve miktar karşıtlığında birleşir; yoksulluk ve düşüklük, az sayma ve bazı yapılarda yokluğa yaklaşan kullanım bu çekirdeğin düzenli uzantılarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sayı, miktar veya ölçünün çok olmayışını bildiren temel anlam için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Çokluğun karşıtı olan sayı ve miktar azlığını doğrudan korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyin sayı veya miktar bakımından çok olmadığının söylendiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Temel azlık durumunu doğal bir Türkçe yapıyla tam olarak verir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Azlığın kişide yoksulluk ve toplumsal düşüklük sonucu doğurduğu bağlamlara özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Yoksulluk ile düşüklük arasındaki kaynakta kurulan uzantıyı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir miktarın veya verilen bir şeyin yetersiz ya da küçük sayıldığı değerlendirme bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Değerlendiren kişinin bir şeyi az sayması anlamını tam olarak korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızca sıklığı çok düşüren veya olumsuzluğu pekiştiren kalıplaşmış yapılarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kalıba bağlı seyrekleşme ve yokluğa yaklaşma değerlerini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol azlığı yoksulluk, düşüklük, az sayma ve kalıba bağlı yokluk değerlerine kadar genişletir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol genel azlığı özellikle mal, yiyecek ve verili miktar örnekleri çevresinde toplar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da bir şeyin sayı veya miktar bakımından çok olmayışını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Temel azlık alanları büyük ölçüde örtüşür; ancak bu kolun değerlendirme, toplumsal sonuç ve kalıba bağlı olumsuzluk uzantıları komşu kartta aynı sınırla kurulmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kolun çekirdeği sayı ve miktar azlığıdır; değersizlik bunun ikincil bir sonucudur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kolun çekirdeği güçsüzlük, aşağılık ve düşünme yetisindeki zayıflıktır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da azlıkla değersizlik veya düşüklük arasında anlam ilişkisi kurabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolda değersizlik azlığın uzantısıdır; komşu kolda ise zayıflık ve aşağılık bağımsız çekirdektir, bu yüzden olağan kullanımda birbirlerinin yerine geçmezler.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol bir şeyin sayıca veya miktarca az oluşunu bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol bir şeyin başını, tepesini veya en üst bölümünü bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Aynı kökün sesçe yakın iki ayrı anlam kolu olmaları dışında ortak çekirdekleri yoktur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Ses benzerliği anlam birliği doğurmaz: biri çokluğun karşıtı olan azlığı, diğeri uzamsal olarak en üstte bulunan baş veya tepeyi adlandırır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; genel azlıkla en yakın örtüşme, değersizlikle kurulan yan ilişki ve aynı kökteki tepe anlamıyla olası karışma en açıklayıcı üç sınır olarak seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: القليل والقِلَّة ضد الكثرة، ويدخل فيه الافتقار والذلة، وتقليل الشيء في العين، واستقلاله، واستعمال القليل للنفي أو للندرة
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس علو الشيء ولا الجرة ولا الحمل ولا الرعدة
branches.source_phrase_ar: القل القليل؛ رماه الله بالقل والذل أي بالقلة والذلة (jamhara)؛ شيء قليل وجمعه قلل؛ قل الشيء يقل قلة؛ قلله في عينه؛ أقل افتقر؛ استقله عده قليلا (sihah)؛ قل الشيء يقل قلة فهو قليل وقلال؛ القل من الرجال الخسيس الدنيء؛ قليلة ولا كثيرة؛ قليلا ما يؤمنون؛ قاللت لفلان؛ تقاللت ما أعطاني (tahdhib)؛ القلة والكثرة يستعملان في الأعداد؛ يكنى بالقلة عن الذلة؛ يكنى بها تارة عن العزة؛ قليل يعبر به عن النفي (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin en üstünü veya başını çekirdek anlam olarak verir; dağın yuvarlak üst bölümü, insan başı ve kılıcın başındaki topuz bu çekirdeğin açık uzmanlaşmalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol uzamsal başı ve en üst parçayı bildirir; sayısal azlık ya da büyük kap anlamını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel baş ve en üst bölüm anlamı ile dağ tepesi, insan başı ve kılıç topuzu gibi yapıya bağlı uzmanlaşmalar ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin başını veya en üst bölümünü bildirir. Dağın üstteki yuvarlak parçası, insan başı ve kılıcın sap ucundaki topuz bu uzamsal çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin veya oluşumun başı ya da en üstte bulunan bölümüdür.
Dağın en üstünde yer alan, kimi tanımda yuvarlak biçimli bölümünü adlandırır.
İnsan başı ile kılıcın sap ucundaki başlık veya topuz da aynı üst ve baş kavramıyla adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir şeyin başı ve en üst bölümü üzerinde birleşir; dağ tepesi temel örnektir, insan başı ile kılıç topuzu da aynı biçimsel ve uzamsal çizgide yer alır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir nesnenin ya da doğal oluşumun en üst bölümünü ve başını kapsayan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Baş olma ile uzamsal olarak en üstte bulunma çekirdeğini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Dağın en üst ve kimi zaman yuvarlak bölümünün adlandırıldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Dağa özgü en üst bölüm uzmanlaşmasını doğrudan korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İnsan başının veya başka bir şeyin baş sayılan üst bölümünün kastedildiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Üst bölümün baş olarak kavranmasını kısa ve doğal biçimde verir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kılıcın sap ucunda bulunan başlık ya da topuz parçası anlatılırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kılıca özgü baş veya üst parça uzmanlaşmasını korur.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol başla ilgili renk, büyüklük, yaralanma, sayım ve alışveriş kullanımlarına kadar uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da insanın veya başka bir şeyin başını ve en üst bölümünü adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Baş ve üst bölüm çekirdekleri yakındır; bu kol tepe ve topuz biçimini öne çıkarırken komşu kol başı daha geniş varlık ve kullanım alanlarında işler.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol insan başını ve kılıç topuzunu da üst veya baş kavramına bağlar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol yüksekliği hörgüç, soy üstünlüğü ve toplumsal onur alanlarına genişletir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da bir şeyin en yüksek, öne çıkan tepe bölümünü anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kol somut baş ve üst parça sınırında kalır; komşu kol fiziksel doruktan toplumsal yüceliğe uzanan daha geniş bir yükseklik alanı kurar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol başı, tepeyi ve en üstte bulunan parçayı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından azlığı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Aynı kökün sesçe yakın iki ayrı anlam kolu olmaları dışında ortak çekirdekleri yoktur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu anlam uzamsal bir üst bölüm adıdır; komşu anlam ise çokluğun karşıtı olan nicelik durumudur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar incelendi; genel baş anlamı, doruk ve yükseklik alanı ve aynı kökteki azlık anlamıyla biçimsel karışma sınırı en yararlı karşılaştırmalar olarak seçildi.

branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس القلة بمعنى الصغر أو العدد القليل، وليس إناء القُلَّة
branches.source_phrase_ar: القلة قلة الجبل وهي القطعة تستدير في أعلاه وهي القنة (jamhara)؛ القلة أعلى الجبل؛ قلة كل شيء أعلاه؛ رأس الإنسان قلة (sihah)؛ قلة كل شيء رأسه؛ قلة الجبل أعلاه؛ قبيعة السيف قلته؛ سيف مقلل (tahdhib)؛ قلة الجبل شعفه (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük bir küp veya iri kap anlamında birleşir; iki kaplık ölçü ve belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler de aynı kap anlamını somutlaştırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol büyük bir kap türünü ve onun ölçü değerini kapsar; nicelik azlığı veya dağ tepesi anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Büyük küp anlamı çekirdektir; belirli bir bölgeye bağlanan kap adı ile iki kaplık ölçü yalnızca kendi yapılardaki uzmanlaşmalardır.

concept_map.definition: Büyük bir küpü veya küpe benzeyen iri kabı bildirir. Belirli bir bölgenin iri küpleri ve iki böyle kabın aldığı miktar bu kap anlamına bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Küpe benzeyen iri kabı adlandıran temel ve en doğal Türkçe karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Kabın küp türünde ve olağandan büyük oluşunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kabın özellikle su alması ve büyük kapasitesi öne çıkarıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Büyük kabı ve kaynakta belirtilen su taşıma kapasitesini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İki kabın kendisinden çok onların aldığı sıvı miktarı ölçü olarak kastedildiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İki büyük kabın kapasitesine dayanan ölçü kullanımını tam olarak korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol kabın özellikle iri oluşunu ve iki kaplık ölçü değerini belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol genel bir küp veya saklama kabını büyüklük koşulu olmadan adlandırabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da küp biçimindeki büyükçe saklama kapları için kullanılabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolda büyük kapasite kurucu bir özelliktir; komşu kartta kap türü öndedir ve aynı ölçü uzantısı bulunmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol büyük bir küpü ve ona dayalı kapasite ölçüsünü bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol bir şeyin başını, tepesini veya en üst bölümünü bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Aynı kökün sesçe yakın iki ayrı anlam kolu olmaları dışında ortak çekirdekleri yoktur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Biri hacimli bir kap ve onun ölçüsüdür; diğeri bir varlığın uzamsal olarak en üstteki parçasıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; büyük küp anlamına en yakın iki kap komşusu ile aynı kökteki tepe anlamından ayrım, sınırı göstermek için yeterli ve yinelenmeyen karşılaştırmalardır.
branches.what_is_ar: القُلَّة إناء كالجرة الكبيرة، ومنها قلال هجر والحباب العظام
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس قلة العدد، وليس رأس الجبل
branches.source_phrase_ar: القلة التي جاءت في الحديث مثل قلال هجر هي جرار عظام (jamhara)؛ القلة إناء للعرب كالجرة الكبيرة؛ قلال هجر شبيهة بالحباب (sihah)؛ قلتين يعني هذه الحباب العظام واحدتها قلة؛ قلال هجر؛ القلة منها تأخذ مزادة من الماء (tahdhib)؛ القلة ما أقله الإنسان من جرة وحب (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

concept_gloss.text: yük kaldırma, yükselme ve yola koyulma
concept_gloss.applicability: Taşıma, yukarı kalkma ve yüklenerek hareket etme çizgilerinin birlikte özetlenmesi gereken kavram haritasında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yük üstlenme, yükselme ve yolculuk için harekete geçme bileşenlerini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin veya başka bir taşıyıcının bir nesnenin ağırlığını üstlenmesi bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yükü kaldırma gücü ile onu fiilen taşıma anlamlarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Göğün yükselmesi veya kuşun uçuşa kalkması gibi yukarı yönlü hareket bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yukarı kalkma ile uçuş için yerden ayrılma değerlerini korur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi hareket ettirip sallandırma, nesnenin bulunduğu yerde kararlı duramaması ve hareketin çıkardığı sesi birlikte verir; bunlar tek bir fiziksel hareket olayının neden, sonuç ve işitsel yönleridir.
